title: Sriram Krishnan：Kimi K3 将改写 AI 行业版图
desc: 白宫前 AI 政策顾问解读 Kimi K3 等开源模型带来的定价、安全与政策冲击。
q: 如果你提供有价值的产品，资本主义会负责处理其余的一切。

qs.en: If you're providing a product of value, capitalism will take care of all the rest.
qs.zh: 如果你提供有价值的产品，资本主义会负责处理其余的一切。
qs.speaker: Sriram Krishnan

qs.en: Number one, I don't think it is great that the leading open weight models or open source models, you know, are not American, right?
qs.zh: 第一，我认为领先的开源权重模型或开源模型，你知道，不是美国的，这并不好，对吧？
qs.speaker: Sriram Krishnan

qs.en: what I believe with that is that open-weight models are inherently secure because when you download a model of Hugging Face, it means you have the entire world being able to take it apart, inspect it, fine-tune it, modify it, look at it in ways that you absolutely cannot if they are closed.
qs.zh: 我对此的信念是，开源权重模型本质上是安全的，因为当你从 Hugging Face 下载一个模型时，这意味着你有全世界的人能够拆解它、检查它、微调它、修改它、以你绝对无法在封闭模型上做到的方式查看它。
qs.speaker: Sriram Krishnan

qs.en: I think the situation which is bad today is that some of these models from other countries can train off American models.
qs.zh: 我认为今天糟糕的情况是，来自其他国家的一些模型可以脱离美国模型进行训练。
qs.speaker: Sriram Krishnan

qs.en: if you look at any American open source model today, they are using Chinese models as a teacher or in a way as a part of the fine tuning process.
qs.zh: 如果你看今天任何美国开源模型，它们都在使用中国模型作为老师或在某种程度上作为微调过程的一部分。
qs.speaker: Sriram Krishnan

qs.en: if you're providing a product of value, capitalism will find a way to make the supply chain work for you.
qs.zh: 如果你提供一个有价值的产品，资本主义会找到一种方法让供应链为你工作。
qs.speaker: Sriram Krishnan

tldr: 白宫前 AI 政策顾问解读 Kimi K3 等开源模型带来的定价、安全与政策冲击。

title: AI 悬崖边？数据中心次级债与 SpaceX 缩水
desc: 本期探讨 AI 经济风险:资本支出悬空、SPV 次级债隐患与 SpaceX 高估值回归。
q: 现在举证责任在怀疑者身上,但一旦你有了令人失望的信息的缓慢渗透,那么举证责任就开始转移到乐观者身上了。

qs.en: right now the burden of proof is on the skeptics, but once you have the slow trickle of disappointing information, then the burden starts to be on the optimists.
qs.zh: 现在举证责任在怀疑者身上,但一旦你有了令人失望的信息的缓慢渗透,那么举证责任就开始转移到乐观者身上了。
qs.speaker: Alex

qs.en: The only way you reach AGI and still lose is if you make that AGI available to others.
qs.zh: 你达到 AGI 却仍然输掉的唯一方式,就是如果你让那个 AGI 可供其他人使用。
qs.speaker: Alex

qs.en: to be abundantly clear, the vast majority of AI data center compute revenue is contingent on the continued ability of two unprofitable, unsustainable AI companies to raise tens or hundreds of billions of dollars a year.
qs.zh: 为了极其明确一点, AI 数据中心算力收入的绝大部分取决于两家不盈利、不可持续的 AI 公司是否有能力继续每年筹集数百亿或数千亿美元。
qs.speaker: Alex

qs.en: for me to be wrong, there will have to be dramatic amounts of AI compute demand, hundreds of billions of worth within the next three years at a time when there is a little more than $120 billion, with 80% or more of that coming from two companies that can only afford it because they have near infinite sums of venture capital behind them.
qs.zh: 如果我错了,在未来三年内,将必须出现大量的 AI 计算需求,价值数千亿美元,而这个时期的 AI 计算收入只比 1200 亿美元多一点,其中 80% 或更多来自两家公司,而这两家公司之所以负担得起,是因为它们背后有近乎无限的风险投资资金。
qs.speaker: Alex

tldr: 本期探讨 AI 经济风险:资本支出悬空、SPV 次级债隐患与 SpaceX 高估值回归。

title: Netflix 产品负责人谈 AI 时代：每个人都能做一切,但卓越的专长不会消失
desc: Elizabeth Stone 分享 AI 如何重塑 Netflix 的团队角色、招聘标准与企业文化——专长不会消失,系统思维与对模糊性的包容成为刚需。
q: 所以,可能是一个智能体编写了代码,或者我帮助进行了分析,而这并不是我的背景,但这并不意味着人们不需要对他们所创造的东西带来的责任负责。

qs.en: So, it can be that an agent wrote the code or I helped to do an analysis when that's not really my background, but it doesn't make people not have the responsibility that comes with what they've created.
qs.zh: 所以,可能是一个智能体编写了代码,或者我帮助进行了分析,而这并不是我的背景,但这并不意味着人们不需要对他们所创造的东西带来的责任负责。
qs.speaker: Elizabeth Stone

qs.en: But I think it would be a mistake to say design and deep design expertise and thinking gets squeezed out, just because we can write code faster, we can do data analysis faster.
qs.zh: 但我认为如果说设计和深刻的设计专业知识及思维因此而被挤出,那将是一个错误,仅仅是因为我们可以更快地编写代码,我们可以更快地进行数据分析。
qs.speaker: Elizabeth Stone

qs.en: The days of very narrow, deep specialization feel more limited to me.
qs.zh: 非常狭窄、深度的专业化日子对我来说感觉更加受限了。
qs.speaker: Elizabeth Stone

qs.en: It's a resistance to do the thing that a lot of bigger companies would do and to feel comfortable in that discomfort very often.
qs.zh: 它是对抗许多大公司会做的事情,并且经常在那种不适中感到舒适。
qs.speaker: Elizabeth Stone

qs.en: Well, the talent density is the non-negotiable.
qs.zh: 嗯,人才密度是不可妥协的。
qs.speaker: Elizabeth Stone

tldr: Elizabeth Stone 分享 AI 如何重塑 Netflix 的团队角色、招聘标准与企业文化——专长不会消失,系统思维与对模糊性的包容成为刚需。

title: OpenClaw创始人：为何80%的应用将消失
desc: OpenClaw 作者谈运行在本地的个人 AI 智能体如何吞掉多数 App、用 CLI 取代 MCP,以及他作为独立开发者的构建哲学。
q: 看起来每个人都在追逐某种集中的上帝智能。而在过去十天左右涌现出来的似乎是群体智能和社区智能。

qs.en: It seems like everyone was chasing sort of the centralized God intelligence. And what has sort of emerged over the past 10 days or so is sort of the swarm intelligence and the community intelligence.
qs.zh: 看起来每个人都在追逐某种集中的上帝智能。而在过去十天左右涌现出来的似乎是群体智能和社区智能。
qs.speaker: Raphael Schaad

qs.en: Even though it’s generalized intelligence, what if it actually is also specialized intelligence?
qs.zh: 即使它是通用智能,如果它实际上也是专用智能呢?
qs.speaker: Peter Steinberger

qs.en: So the companies try to bind you to their data silo.
qs.zh: 所以公司试图把你绑定到他们的数据孤岛。
qs.speaker: Peter Steinberger

qs.en: No, just have CLIs. The bot really is good at Unix. You can have as many as you want and it just works.
qs.zh: 不,只需要 CLI。机器人真的擅长 Unix。你可以想要多少就有多少,它就能工作。
qs.speaker: Peter Steinberger

qs.en: No sane human tries to call MCP manually.
qs.zh: 没有理智的人类会尝试手动调用 MCP。
qs.speaker: Peter Steinberger

qs.en: it had to be a loner from some tiny country far away from Silicon Valley to bring all of this upon us.
qs.zh: 必须是一个来自离硅谷很远的某个小国家的独行侠带给我们这一切。
qs.speaker: Raphael Schaad

tldr: OpenClaw 作者谈运行在本地的个人 AI 智能体如何吞掉多数 App、用 CLI 取代 MCP,以及他作为独立开发者的构建哲学。

title: PM 如何用 Claude 把生产力提升 10 倍：全栈实战
desc: 从模型选型到构建个人幕僚长智能体,用 Claude 全栈打造 PM 生产力引擎。
q: 我认为这是大多数 PM 投入不足的一层,正是这一层让 Claude 从一个通用的聊天机器人变成真正了解你的上下文。

qs.en: the layer that i think most pms under invest in it's this layer that makes claude go from being a generic chatbot to actually knowing your context
qs.zh: 我认为这是大多数 PM 投入不足的一层,正是这一层让 Claude 从一个通用的聊天机器人变成真正了解你的上下文。
qs.speaker: Jyothi Nookula

qs.en: building is easy now taste is what is important for us to develop
qs.zh: 现在构建变得容易了,品味才是我们需要培养的重要东西。
qs.speaker: Jyothi Nookula

qs.en: previously if you see one product manager works with eight engineers now it's like two product managers one engineer so the roles are also like collapsing quickly
qs.zh: 以前一个产品经理配八个工程师,现在变成了两个产品经理配一个工程师,所以角色也在迅速合并。
qs.speaker: Jyothi Nookula

qs.en: am I just taking the first thing that the AI tells me as like this is great and wrapping it up or am I looking through things to say okay this is good but what about this edge case
qs.zh: 我是不是把 AI 告诉我的第一件事就当作『这很棒』然后直接收尾,还是我在审视这些事情并说『好吧这很好,但是这种边缘情况怎么办』
qs.speaker: Jyothi Nookula

qs.en: don't build them as projects treat them as products like find problems in your area find problems that are finicky enough for you to want to go build a solution go build solution and see who else wants something like this have them come and use your product
qs.zh: 不要把它们当成项目来做,要把它们当成产品。去你所在的领域发现问题,找那些足够棘手、让你想去构建解决方案的问题,去构建解决方案,然后看看还有谁想要这样的东西,让他们来用你的产品。
qs.speaker: Jyothi Nookula

qs.en: this is where you're not just building an agent you're actually building another evaluator to go break this agent in different ways
qs.zh: 这就是你不仅仅是在构建一个智能体,你实际上是在构建另一个评估器,用不同的方式去攻破这个智能体。
qs.speaker: Jyothi Nookula

tldr: 从模型选型到构建个人幕僚长智能体,用 Claude 全栈打造 PM 生产力引擎。

title: 科技圈情绪调查：一半人狂喜，一半人煎熬
desc: 6000人调查揭示科技圈因AI一分为二，倦怠激增、乐观骤降，但经理和小公司是破局关键。
q: 而每次你把这种负担推卸给你最喜欢的 AI 模型时，你都在降低那个基线，而你的思考和判断正在旁观。

qs.en: And every time you offload that to your favorite AI model, you are lowering that baseline and your thinking and your judgment is watching.
qs.zh: 而每次你把这种负担推卸给你最喜欢的 AI 模型时，你都在降低那个基线，而你的思考和判断正在旁观。
qs.speaker: Noam Segal

qs.en: Tech is manic. Half out of touch, clinging to the bandwagon, pouring into the over hype. The other half are exhausted by the first half.
qs.zh: 科技是躁狂的。一半人与现实脱节，死死抱住流行趋势，投入到过度宣传中。另一半人则被这一半人弄得精疲力竭。
qs.speaker: Noam Segal

qs.en: The productivity gains are real, but the quality of the work and the sharpness of the person producing it are taking a hit.
qs.zh: 生产力的提升是真实的，但工作的质量以及生产它的人的敏锐度正在受到打击。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: The speed AI unlocked got plowed straight back into expectations. Every game becomes the new baseline and the people expected to hit it are running out of room to breathe.
qs.zh: AI 解锁的速度直接被投入到期望之中。每一项成就都成为新的基准，而那些被期望达到这一基准的人正几乎没有喘息的空间。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: People are feeling how AI is raising bars in ways that aren't sustainable.
qs.zh: 人们感觉到 AI 正在以一种不可持续的方式提高门槛。
qs.speaker: Noam Segal

qs.en: I doubt it's going away. It's the worst it's ever going to be today. It's only getting better.
qs.zh: 我怀疑它会消失。它今天是最糟糕的。它只会变得更好。
qs.speaker: Noam Segal

qs.en: We're in the second inning of a massive shift. No one knows how it will end, but all you can do is keep taking at bats.
qs.zh: 我们正处于一场大规模变革的第二局。没有人知道它将如何结束，但你所能做的就是继续挥棒击球。
qs.speaker: Noam Segal

tldr: 6000人调查揭示科技圈因AI一分为二，倦怠激增、乐观骤降，但经理和小公司是破局关键。

title: 用 AI 武装技术型 PM：Codex 工作流全解析
desc: 设计师 Meng To 展示如何用 Codex 搭建插件与技能生态，转型为掌控智能体舰队的超级个体。
q: 因为有了 AI，你不再需要害怕创办公司了，因为 AI 可以为你处理所有的文书工作，为你处理所有的会计工作，所有那些无聊的事情。

qs.en: because ai you don't need to be scared of starting a company anymore because ai can take care of all the paperwork for you all the accounting for you all the the boring stuff
qs.zh: 因为有了 AI，你不再需要害怕创办公司了，因为 AI 可以为你处理所有的文书工作，为你处理所有的会计工作，所有那些无聊的事情。
qs.speaker: Meng To

qs.en: you know best because like any business rule is that you have to be the one who knows this topic the best otherwise you don't have any leverage
qs.zh: 你最清楚，因为就像任何商业规则一样，你必须成为那个最了解这个主题的人，否则你就没有任何筹码。
qs.speaker: Meng To

qs.en: then let ai be your amplifier magnifier so that you can quickly make these micro decisions and you can deploy a fleet of agents
qs.zh: 然后让 AI 成为你的放大器、扩音器，这样你就可以快速做出这些微观决策，并且你可以部署一支智能体舰队。
qs.speaker: Meng To

qs.en: you don't have to do that anymore you have an army of agents
qs.zh: 你不必再那样做了，你有一支智能体大军。
qs.speaker: Meng To

qs.en: eventually you will get fired because ai will replace everyone at some point or we will find new ways to do our job
qs.zh: 最终你会被解雇，因为 AI 会在某个时间点取代所有人，或者我们将找到新的工作方式。
qs.speaker: Meng To

tldr: 设计师 Meng To 展示如何用 Codex 搭建插件与技能生态，转型为掌控智能体舰队的超级个体。

title: Adam Mosseri：AI 时代的团队重组与产品品味
desc: Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 聊 AI 如何重塑团队、品味与推荐算法。
q: 我实际上非常看好设计师，因为他们往往有品味，我认为这是更难想象被自动化掉的事情

qs.en: i'm actually pretty long on design or designers because they tend to have taste and i think that is something that is much more difficult to imagine being automated away
qs.zh: 我实际上非常看好设计师，因为他们往往有品味，我认为这是更难想象被自动化掉的事情
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: if strategy can't be like be the best or be amazing it has to be controversial that you have to be a reasonable person should be able to disagree with it because otherwise you're probably just trying to compete on raw execution
qs.zh: 如果战略不能是最好的或惊人的，它必须是具有争议的，一个理性的人应该能够不同意它，因为否则你可能只是试图在原始执行上竞争
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: in a world where there's an abundance of synthetic content i actually think people are going to seek out creativity and authenticity and people more not less
qs.zh: 在一个合成内容丰富的世界里，实际上我认为人们会更多而不是更少地寻求创造力、真实性和人
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: i think taste matters a ton uh so in a world where it's easier to build things it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place
qs.zh: 我认为品味非常重要，所以在一个更容易构建事物的世界里，更重要的是确保你的时间花在弄清楚你首先应该构建什么上
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: i think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is
qs.zh: 我认为人们假设算法对每个人的兴趣和偏好有更详细的语义理解，但实际并没有那么多
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: i don't think we should judge content based on the tool that made it um i think we should judge it based on the content the point of view the person behind the content
qs.zh: 我不认为我们应该根据制造它的工具来评判内容，我认为我们应该根据内容、观点、内容背后的人来评判它
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: if you do a pure chronological feed the incentive for everybody is to just post as much as possible because it will always be at the top of everyone who follows you's feed as soon as you post
qs.zh: 如果你做一个纯粹的按时间顺序的信息流，每个人的激励就是尽可能多地发布内容，因为一旦你发布，它总是会位于每个关注你的人的信息流的顶部
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: you can't you can't you can't launch something to three billion people and not test it first but you can't test something at our scale and not expect people to cover it
qs.zh: 你不能你不能你不能向三十亿人发布某样东西而不先测试它，但你不能在我们的规模上测试某样东西而不期望人们去报道它
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

qs.en: i would much rather have backlashes like that every couple years but continue to evolve and continue to stay relevant than the alternative which would have been like we didn't have video we didn't have dms we didn't have stories we didn't have ranking
qs.zh: 我宁愿每隔几年遇到像那样的抵制，但继续进化并保持相关性，也不愿要替代方案，那就像是我们没有视频，我们没有私信，我们没有 Stories，我们没有排名
qs.speaker: Adam Mosseri

tldr: Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 聊 AI 如何重塑团队、品味与推荐算法。

title: 从避战大模型到押注智能体：Modal 的推理基础设施进化史
desc: Modal CTO 剖析从开发者体验转向智能体体验的推理云进化路径。
q: 我们在 2023 年 5 月就构建了沙箱，在任何人甚至知道这将成为一件事之前。

qs.en: we built sandboxes in May of 2023 before anyone was even knew this was going to be a thing.
qs.zh: 我们在 2023 年 5 月就构建了沙箱，在任何人甚至知道这将成为一件事之前。
qs.speaker: Akshat Bubna

qs.en: which is why would you have an agent read through hundreds of Kubernetes files and write YAML that's not even typed when it can basically make a couple of changes in a decorator
qs.zh: 这就是为什么你要让一个智能体去阅读数百个 Kubernetes 文件并编写甚至没有类型的 YAML，而它基本上可以在一个装饰器中做几个更改
qs.speaker: Akshat Bubna

qs.en: When you're doing rollouts, you sometimes need 100,000 sandboxes.
qs.zh: 当你在做 rollouts 的时候，你有时需要十万个沙箱。
qs.speaker: Akshat Bubna

qs.en: improving kernel only give you like few percentage points improvement and increasing except lengths literally is multiplicative decrease in two to four x
qs.zh: 改进内核只给你几个百分点的提升，而增加接受长度实际上是 2 到 4 倍的乘法性减少
qs.speaker: Akshat Bubna

qs.en: This is one thing we've kind of stayed away from is providing an API for models
qs.zh: 这是我们一直有所回避的一件事，就是为模型提供 API
qs.speaker: Akshat Bubna

tldr: Modal CTO 剖析从开发者体验转向智能体体验的推理云进化路径。

title: Gusto CTO 的极简实验:5 人 10 周凭感觉编程造出 AI 产品
desc: 大公司 CTO 用无文档、无会议、无 PM 的极简流程带 5 人团队开发新 AI 产品。
q: 我们把一切都归零了。我们没有会议,没有技术规格,没有 Figma。我们没有用来追踪故事或工作的 Jira 看板。我们没有站会,没有回顾会。

qs.en: just zeroed everything out we had no meetings we had no tech specs we had no figmas. we had no JIRA board where we track stories or tracked work. We had no stand-ups, no retros.
qs.zh: 我们把一切都归零了。我们没有会议,没有技术规格,没有 Figma。我们没有用来追踪故事或工作的 Jira 看板。我们没有站会,没有回顾会。
qs.speaker: Eddie Kim

qs.en: I think you actually have to go to these teams and say, we want you to work in this way, where you don't do any docs, no figmas, no tech specs.
qs.zh: 我认为你必须去这些团队并说,我们希望你们以这种方式工作,你们不做任何文档,不做 Figma,不做技术规格。
qs.speaker: Eddie Kim

qs.en: if you actually produce a doc or figma like you will get a slap on the wrist because we explicitly don't want you to do that
qs.zh: 如果你真的写了文档或做了 Figma,你会受到警告,因为我们明确不希望你们做那个
qs.speaker: Eddie Kim

qs.en: I think it's very hard to build great AI products if you are not spending all your time using AI products right now.
qs.zh: 我认为如果你现在没有把所有时间都用来使用 AI 产品,就很难构建出优秀的 AI 产品。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: even that's not a big investment across a company of a thousand in R&D. You're going to have like two or three of those, I think, meaningfully change the trajectory of the business.
qs.zh: 即便这样,对于一家拥有上千名研发人员的公司来说,这也不是一笔大投资。我认为,只要有两三个这样的项目,就能有意义地改变企业的轨迹。
qs.speaker: Eddie Kim

qs.en: on average is your engineering teams PRS getting faster review than their non-engineering teams PRS and like across the board people are like yeah of course they are like that is an anti-pattern you need to prioritize reviewing these non-engineering PRS just as high as you do your engineering ones
qs.zh: 平均而言,你们工程团队的 PR 是否比非工程团队的 PR 得到更快的审查?全面的人们都说是的,当然是。这是一个反模式,你需要优先审查这些非工程的 PR,就像你审查工程 PR 一样高
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: you don't touch the outputs of agent code. You only get to touch the inputs. You only get to reprompt. You don't get to rewrite the code.
qs.zh: 你不要碰 agent 代码的输出。你只能碰输入。你只能重新提示。你不能重写代码。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: And that's actually a very interesting model where maybe docs exist, but they're for the agents, not for the humans.
qs.zh: 这其实是一个很有趣的模型,也许文档是存在的,但它们是给智能体的,不是给人类的。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

tldr: 大公司 CTO 用无文档、无会议、无 PM 的极简流程带 5 人团队开发新 AI 产品。

title: AI 时代的产品团队：Laurel CPO 的公司操作系统与「超级个体」实战
desc: Laurel CPO 分享如何用 AI 技能库构建公司操作系统，让非工程师也能端到端交付产品功能。
q: 我认为这是公司最挣扎的事情，也就是你有这些人，他们是这 1% 的 AI 用户。他们在修补他们的工作流程，他们高度 AI 化，然后你有你知道组织中其余 90% 到 99% 的人不确定该什么时候使用什么。

qs.en: I think that's the biggest thing that companies struggle with, which is you got these people who are these 1% AI users. they're tinkering with their workflows they're highly AI pilled and then you have the you know 90 to 99 percent of the rest of the organization who isn't sure what to use when
qs.zh: 我认为这是公司最挣扎的事情，也就是你有这些人，他们是这 1% 的 AI 用户。他们在修补他们的工作流程，他们高度 AI 化，然后你有你知道组织中其余 90% 到 99% 的人不确定该什么时候使用什么。
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

qs.en: if everyone's running in different directions, even if you're running incredibly fast, you're not really going to get anywhere.
qs.zh: 如果每个人都在朝不同的方向奔跑，即使你跑得非常快，你也不会真的到达任何地方。
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

qs.en: I think so yeah I mean I've had hundreds of people and today I have five PMs and four designers and there isn't a real reason to grow that because again like when you add more people you add more coordination costs
qs.zh: 我想是的，是的，我的意思是，我曾经手下有几百人，而今天我有 5 个 PM 和 4 个设计师，并且没有真正的理由去增加人数，因为就像当你增加更多人，你就增加了更多协调成本
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

qs.en: I think it's because 1PM can do so much more than ever before, but there aren't that many of them who are that skilled, that have that judgment, who are AI-pilled, who fearlessly are going through all of these pieces
qs.zh: 我认为这是因为 1 个 PM 可以做比以往任何时候多得多的事情，但没有那么多有这种技能的人，有那种判断力的人，是 AI 化的人，无畏地经历所有这些环节的人
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

qs.en: The empty state that we're working on here it's the hardest part to get right is definitely not the engineering the hardest part to get right is not even the design it's the content
qs.zh: 我们在这里正在处理的空状态，最难做对的部分绝对不是工程，最难做对的部分甚至不是设计，而是内容
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

qs.en: So I think it's really finding who I call the orchestrators, the people who are big picture in terms of their thinking but down to the detail in terms of their execution.
qs.zh: 所以我认为这真的在于寻找我称之为编排者的人，那些在思维上有大局观但在执行上落实到细节的人。
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

qs.en: a lot of times when you say it's everyone's responsibility it's no one's responsibility and so what we have at Laurel is we actually have an AI operations team
qs.zh: 很多时候当你说这是每个人的责任时，那就是没有任何人的责任，所以我们在 Laurel 所做的是我们实际上有一个 AI 运营团队
qs.speaker: Jiaona Zhang

tldr: Laurel CPO 分享如何用 AI 技能库构建公司操作系统，让非工程师也能端到端交付产品功能。

title: Databricks 的智能体平台与数据库「圣杯」：Reynold Xin 与 Matei Zaharia 的技术蓝图
desc: 两位创始人详解智能体平台 Omnigen、打通交易与分析的 LTAP，以及从零重写的数据库引擎。
q: 我让一个智能体去调试某个东西,它花了 500 美元,因为它决定读取大量日志文件并消耗大量 token。

qs.en: I asked an agent to debug something and it spent $500 because it decided to read a lot of log files and burn a lot of tokens.
qs.zh: 我让一个智能体去调试某个东西,它花了 500 美元,因为它决定读取大量日志文件并消耗大量 token。
qs.speaker: Matei Zaharia

qs.en: Imagine our thing wasn't open. We had some kind of agent hosting thing, but it's not open. And then there is an open one. Which one is going to win in the long run?
qs.zh: 想象一下我们的东西不是开放的。我们有某种智能体托管的东西,但它不是开放的。然后有一个开放的。从长远来看哪一个会赢?
qs.speaker: Matei Zaharia

qs.en: CDC is one of the most boring, but one of the most fundamental operations powering modern society.
qs.zh: CDC 是最无聊的之一,但也是驱动现代社会的最基础的操作之一。
qs.speaker: Reynold Xin

qs.en: It should be called continuous data corruption because you might change your schema on your LTP database and then the CDC pipeline fails to handle the schema change.
qs.zh: 说它应该被称为持续数据损坏,因为你可能会在你的 LTP 数据库上更改你的模式,然后 CDC 管道无法处理模式变更。
qs.speaker: Reynold Xin

qs.en: after 10 years of organic evolution that way, it becomes a gigantic pile of shit.
qs.zh: 经过十年那样有机的演化,它就变成了一大堆像屎一样的代码。
qs.speaker: Reynold Xin

qs.en: We think you can get 99% of what you need by unifying the storage.
qs.zh: 我们认为你可以通过统一存储来获得你需要的 99%。
qs.speaker: Reynold Xin

qs.en: But the open data format have won.
qs.zh: 但开放数据格式已经赢了。
qs.speaker: Reynold Xin

qs.en: it's probably like 100x cheaper than those frontier models and still better.
qs.zh: 它可能比那些前沿模型便宜大约 100 倍,而且仍然更好。
qs.speaker: Matei Zaharia

qs.en: Vector database should have never been a separate category.
qs.zh: 向量数据库本不应该是一个单独的类别。
qs.speaker: Reynold Xin

tldr: 两位创始人详解智能体平台 Omnigen、打通交易与分析的 LTAP，以及从零重写的数据库引擎。

title: 让 AI 智能体不「越界」:Gray Swan 的红队测试与安全护栏
desc: CMU学者创办Gray Swan,通过社区与自动化红队测试找出AI漏洞,并用专用模型Signal拦截提示注入,守护企业AI部署。
q: 如果你在每个人都在使用的智能体中发现漏洞,像 Codex 和 Cloud Code 这样的东西,你现在实际上基本上就可以拥有一种新的漏洞利用,一类新的漏洞利用。

qs.en: if you find vulnerabilities in the agents that everyone uses, right, things like Codex and Cloud Code, you can actually start to now essentially have a new exploit, a new class of exploit.
qs.zh: 如果你在每个人都在使用的智能体中发现漏洞,像 Codex 和 Cloud Code 这样的东西,你现在实际上基本上就可以拥有一种新的漏洞利用,一类新的漏洞利用。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

qs.en: frontier models are extremely bad at automated red teaming because they have a lot of safeguards built into them.
qs.zh: 前沿模型在自动化红队测试方面极其糟糕,因为它们内置了大量的保障措施。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

qs.en: It's some alien intelligence that is... Vastly different.
qs.zh: 它是某种外星智能,它是……截然不同。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

qs.en: It's hilarious that humans are ranked number four of all the models.
qs.zh: 人类在所有模型中排名第四,这很搞笑。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

qs.en: you make a model bigger and bigger, it does not necessarily get better inherently at resisting jailbreaks.
qs.zh: 如果你把一个模型做得越来越大,它本质上不一定变得更擅长抵抗越狱。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

qs.en: ingesting untrusted data, having access to private information, and having the ability to exfiltrate it, those are the things that together really form a risk.
qs.zh: 摄取不可信的数据,访问私有信息,以及拥有将其泄露出去的能力,这些才是真正共同构成风险的事情。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

qs.en: you can have your agent write secure code. You don't have to write secure code.
qs.zh: 你可以让你的智能体编写安全的代码。你不必编写安全的代码。
qs.speaker: Zico Kolter

tldr: CMU学者创办Gray Swan,通过社区与自动化红队测试找出AI漏洞,并用专用模型Signal拦截提示注入,守护企业AI部署。

title: 当代码量暴涨8倍:Anthropic工程负责人谈AI时代的团队重构
desc: Fiona Fung分享在代码量暴涨8倍后,如何用异步智能体、验证机制与新管理者制度重塑工程团队。
q: 对于任何你知道存在恐惧的事情,我的建议是拥抱它并问自己,好吧,有什么我能做的吗,什么在我的控制范围内。

qs.en: for anything that you know that there is a fear my advice is kind of lean in and ask okay is there some what can I do about it what is within my control
qs.zh: 对于任何你知道存在恐惧的事情,我的建议是拥抱它并问自己,好吧,有什么我能做的吗,什么在我的控制范围内。
qs.speaker: Fiona Fung

qs.en: Customers will use your product in ways that you did not intend for good or for bad.
qs.zh: 客户会以你没有意图的方式使用你的产品,无论好坏。
qs.speaker: Fiona Fung

qs.en: don't first take motion for progress
qs.zh: 不要首先把动静误认为是进步。
qs.speaker: Fiona Fung

qs.en: I started this hey let's have a concept of what's bad versus what's sad and bad is like a very bad irrecoverable error and sad is something that's kind of like a pain point recoverable
qs.zh: 我开始引入这个概念,让我们区分什么是坏的与什么是悲的,坏是非常糟糕的不可恢复的错误,悲是某种痛点但可恢复。
qs.speaker: Fiona Fung

qs.en: after a while we felt it could start being a lonely experience because we all started just working with our agents so much.
qs.zh: 过了一段时间,我们感觉这可能开始变成一种孤独的体验,因为我们都开始如此频繁地与我们的智能体一起工作了。
qs.speaker: Fiona Fung

tldr: Fiona Fung分享在代码量暴涨8倍后,如何用异步智能体、验证机制与新管理者制度重塑工程团队。

title: Zynga 创始人 Mark Pincus：想做出伟大产品，先学会「合法地抄袭」
desc: Zynga 创始人分享消费产品的核心方法论「Proven, Better, New」：大胆借鉴被验证的模式，克制野心从小处起步，并果断放弃平庸的 B+ 想法。
q: 你的直觉 95% 的时候是对的，而你的想法 75% 的时候是错的，或者充其量只有 25% 的时候是对的。

qs.en: Your instincts are right 95% of the time, your ideas are wrong 75% or at best right 25% of the time.
qs.zh: 你的直觉 95% 的时候是对的，而你的想法 75% 的时候是错的，或者充其量只有 25% 的时候是对的。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: If you're truly ambitious, burn your resume.
qs.zh: 如果你真的有雄心壮志，就烧掉你的简历。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: If you define your ambition in the eyes of your consumer, not your peers, you're not trying to win awards and respect from your peers, you're trying to win the hearts and minds of nurses in Indiana, like for Farmville, you're going to define innovation differently and you're not going to worry about whether...
qs.zh: 如果你根据消费者的眼光而非同行的眼光来定义你的抱负，你不是试图赢得奖项和同行的尊重，你是试图赢得印第安纳州护士的心和思想，就像 Farmville 一样，你会以不同的方式定义创新，而且你不会担心是否……
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: If we're too ambitious at the outset and too ambitious and visionary about the product we want to build, then we will probably miss product market fit because we won't start at a small enough, humble enough place
qs.zh: 如果我们一开始太雄心勃勃，对我们要构建的产品愿景太远大，那我们很可能会错过产品市场契合度，因为我们不会从一个足够微小、足够谦逊的地方开始
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: But I'd say my ambition came down to a 1000 ft altitude, not a 100,000 ft. And that was the key to that being successful.
qs.zh: 但我想说我的雄心降到了 1000 英尺的高度，而不是 10 万英尺。那是成功的关键。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: The paradox is the more ambitious you are that the more humble you should be in the smaller place you should be willing to start.
qs.zh: 悖论在于，你越有雄心，你就应该越谦逊，你应该愿意从更小的地方开始。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: I think that too many founders and teams keep going with the hope that this next release is going to do something magical.
qs.zh: 我认为太多的创始人和团队继续抱着希望，认为下一个版本会带来奇迹。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: If you're asking whether or not your product is an A, it's not an A and you're full of hope.
qs.zh: 如果你在问你的产品是否是 A，那它就不是 A，而你充满了希望。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: When you have lightning in a bottle, when you have true signal, everything works.
qs.zh: 当你拥有了瓶中闪电，当你拥有真正的信号时，一切都行得通。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: So build it wrong before you know it's right.
qs.zh: 所以在知道它是对的之前先把它构建错。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: I think AI is being used more to build one idea in three months than a hundred ideas in a day.
qs.zh: 我认为 AI 更多被用来在三个月内构建一个想法，而不是一天内构建 100 个想法。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: I believe that we have beyond a latent demand for social, we are being social online. We are on Snapchat and Instagram and TikTok, but I believe it's lost the adrenaline.
qs.zh: 我相信我们对社交有着超越潜在需求的需求，我们正在线上进行社交。我们在 Snapchat、Instagram 和 TikTok 上，但我认为它失去了肾上腺素。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: Today we're all hanging out on our Claude on our GPT, but there's no cocktail party.
qs.zh: 如今我们都挂在 Claude 上，挂在 GPT 上，但没有鸡尾酒会。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: My challenge to your listeners is figure out how to make it rowdy, figure out how to make that cocktail party social and socially productive and you will probably find gold there.
qs.zh: 我对你听众的挑战是，弄清楚如何让它变得喧闹，弄清楚如何让那个鸡尾酒会变得社交化并具有社交生产力，你很可能会在那里找到金矿。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: If you're just building this product and hoping they will come, hoping it'll spread virally or word of mouth, that's hope strategy, not a belief strategy.
qs.zh: 如果你只是建造这个产品并希望它们会来，希望它能病毒式传播或口碑传播，那是希望策略，而不是信念策略。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: Even if you don't operate the ship or the factory that well, I'd rather that you picked the right product, the right strategy than your phenomenal execution, or inspiring people or managing.
qs.zh: 即使你没有很好地经营这艘船或工厂，我宁愿你选择了正确的产品、正确的战略，而不是你非凡的执行力，或者鼓舞人心或管理。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

qs.en: Because being in the right body of water matters more than the right boat, and a great boat in a dead lake bed isn't going anywhere.
qs.zh: 因为在正确的水域里比拥有一艘正确的船更重要，而在干涸的湖床上的一艘好船哪儿也去不了。
qs.speaker: Mark Pincus

tldr: Zynga 创始人分享消费产品的核心方法论「Proven, Better, New」：大胆借鉴被验证的模式，克制野心从小处起步，并果断放弃平庸的 B+ 想法。

title: iPod之父Tony Fadell：反直觉的产品课
desc: iPod与Nest之父Tony Fadell谈伟大产品背后的直觉、取舍与反共识勇气。
q: 因为如果你一路尝试做数据驱动的决策，你要么不是在做差异化的产品，因为你在从其他东西获取数据，要么你只是在得到废话数据，对吧。

qs.en: Because if you try to do data-driven decisions all the way along, you're either not doing a differentiated product because you're taking data from another thing, or you're just getting just bullshit data, right.
qs.zh: 因为如果你一路尝试做数据驱动的决策，你要么不是在做差异化的产品，因为你在从其他东西获取数据，要么你只是在得到废话数据，对吧。
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: The mantra was, "Steve, if we don't have Windows connectivity, the iPod doesn't cost $349.
qs.zh: 信条是，“Steve，如果我们没有 Windows 连接性，iPod 就不是卖 349 美元。
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: You're building on a really crusty foundation.
qs.zh: 你正在一个非常脆弱的基础上构建。
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: You're getting short-term gain for very, very long-term laws.
qs.zh: 你正在获得短期的收益，却是为了非常、非常长期的代价。
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: And then if you looked at the code, anybody who looked at the code who's a real software architect and engineer threw up, they were like, "It made what?"
qs.zh: 然后如果你看了代码，任何看过代码的真正的软件架构师和工程师都呕吐了，他们就像，「它造了什么？」
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: The technology's in service of the customer, not we're going to jam the technology down the customer's throat.
qs.zh: 技术是为客户服务的，而不是我们要把技术硬塞给客户。
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: We can use the machines, but don't cognitively surrender.
qs.zh: 我们可以使用机器，但不要在认知上投降。
qs.speaker: Tony Fadell

qs.en: Because it's so easy to build, the things that stand out are the things that are really well thought through.
qs.zh: 因为它太容易构建了，所以脱颖而出的东西是那些真正经过深思熟虑的东西。
qs.speaker: Lenny

tldr: iPod与Nest之父Tony Fadell谈伟大产品背后的直觉、取舍与反共识勇气。

title: Satya Nadella 谈 AI 时代平台逻辑:私有评估是最大 IP
desc: 微软 CEO 畅谈 AI 时代的平台生态战略:从模型血统到智能体重塑企业价值。
q: 拥有私有评估可能是最大的知识产权。

qs.en: Having private evals may be the biggest IP.
qs.zh: 拥有私有评估可能是最大的知识产权。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

qs.en: I can just come and have you all just worship at the altar of one model. But that's not a developer conference.
qs.zh: 我可以直接来让大家就在一个模型的祭坛前顶礼膜拜。但那不是开发者大会。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

qs.en: you should always acquire something if the marginal cost of building and maintaining something on your own is higher.
qs.zh: 如果自己构建和维护某样东西的边际成本更高,你就应该总是去获取它。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

qs.en: You saw that I talked about how we built in the last 15 months more Azure capacity than we built in the first 15 years.
qs.zh: 你看到我谈到了我们如何在过去15个月里建成了比我们前15年建成的更多的Azure容量。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

qs.en: if somebody had come to us and said, four billion people are going to get up in the morning and start typing, my model would have been, we need four billion typists, but We're not doing typing. We're doing knowledge work.
qs.zh: 如果有人来找我们说,四十亿人早上起床后会开始打字,我的模型会是,我们需要四十亿打字员,但我们不是在做打字。我们是在做知识工作。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

qs.en: I think the world is going to be very skeptical of tech and tech companies that say, trust us, we've got it, the future is going to be glorious. We have to deliver tangible benefits.
qs.zh: 我认为世界将会非常怀疑那些说“相信我们,我们搞定了,未来将会是辉煌的”的科技和科技公司。我们必须交付切实的好处。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

qs.en: In fact, what I use to serve an inbox or a mailbox cannot be used to serve an agent.
qs.zh: 事实上,我用来服务收件箱或邮箱的东西不能用来服务智能体。
qs.speaker: Satya Nadella

tldr: 微软 CEO 畅谈 AI 时代的平台生态战略:从模型血统到智能体重塑企业价值。

title: Dan Shipper 的未来工作预测：别等 AI 末日，用 Codex 重塑一切
desc: Every CEO 预测工作将分化为超级智能体与本机 AI 两条主线，SaaS 不会消亡，PM 与设计师将迎来黄金时代。
q: 我认为 SaaS 末日论是愚蠢的。

qs.en: I think the SaaSpocalypse is dumb.
qs.zh: 我认为 SaaS 末日论是愚蠢的。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: I would buy SaaS stocks right now.
qs.zh: 我现在会买入 SaaS 股票。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: What agents do is increase the number of users of SaaS, not get rid of it.
qs.zh: 智能体所做的是增加 SaaS 的用户数量，而不是摆脱它。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: Automation is a lie, in the sense that every time you automate something, in order to make sure the automation is working well you need a human on top of it making sure that it's working well.
qs.zh: 自动化是个谎言，从某种意义上说，每次你自动化某样东西时，为了确保自动化运行良好，你需要一个人在上面确保它运行良好。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: I'm simultaneously extremely AI pilled and very bullish on humans.
qs.zh: 我同时极其 AI 信奉（pilled）且非常看好人类。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: What models do in general is they make yesterday's human competence cheap.
qs.zh: 模型总体上做的是让昨天的人类能力变得廉价。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: We speed ran the CLI era.
qs.zh: 我们速通了 CLI 时代。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: It was nice while it lasted, but I think CLIs are over.
qs.zh: 它在持续期间很不错，但我认为 CLI 已经过时了。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: Your company's only going to go as far as your CEO goes in AI and it's not something you can delegate.
qs.zh: 你的公司的发展程度只能达到你的 CEO 在 AI 方面的发展程度，而且这是你不能委托的事情。
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

qs.en: I think the edge of AI is wherever AI meets a real human doing something
qs.zh: 我认为 AI 的前沿是 AI 遇到真实的人做事情的地方
qs.speaker: Dan Shipper

tldr: Every CEO 预测工作将分化为超级智能体与本机 AI 两条主线，SaaS 不会消亡，PM 与设计师将迎来黄金时代。

title: 赋予AI智能体计算机——Daytona创始人Ivan Burazin
desc: Daytona 为智能体打造毫秒级启动的裸金属沙箱,迎击 RL 训练与后台智能体的算力新挑战。
q: 但如果你想一次启动 50,000 个,我们现在大约需要 75 秒。

qs.en: But if you want to spin up 50,000 at once, we are now at about 75 seconds.
qs.zh: 但如果你想一次启动 50,000 个,我们现在大约需要 75 秒。
qs.speaker: Ivan Burazin

qs.en: unpredictable workloads that we've never had before in human computer or human
qs.zh: 我们以前从未有过这种不可预测的工作负载,无论是在人类计算机还是人类
qs.speaker: Ivan Burazin

qs.en: The PC market is about equal to the cloud market.
qs.zh: PC 市场大约等于云市场。
qs.speaker: Ivan Burazin

qs.en: the market is adding premium to SaaS vendors that are reselling tokens.
qs.zh: 市场正在给那些转售 token 的 SaaS 供应商增加溢价。
qs.speaker: Ivan Burazin

qs.en: The entire infrastructure market is growing 40% plus or minus month over month.
qs.zh: 整个基础设施市场每个月以 40% 左右的速度增长。
qs.speaker: Ivan Burazin

tldr: Daytona 为智能体打造毫秒级启动的裸金属沙箱,迎击 RL 训练与后台智能体的算力新挑战。

title: 《精益创业》作者 Eric Ries 新作导读：好公司为什么会「变坏」
desc: 创始人如何用法律结构和使命驱动，保护公司免受短期利润的侵蚀。
q: 摧毁它们的东西不是竞争。

qs.en: The thing that destroyed them was not competition.
qs.zh: 摧毁它们的东西不是竞争。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: If you don't get this right, no other decision you make about your company will matter for the long term because you're not going to be the one making it.
qs.zh: 如果你搞不定这个，那么你关于公司做出的其他决定都没有长期意义，因为你不会是做决定的那个人。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: It is always too early until it's too late.
qs.zh: 在太晚之前，总是太早。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: Success will not protect you because success is what makes you a target.
qs.zh: 成功不会保护你，因为成功正是让你成为靶子的原因。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: Their intervention ultimately created more than $500 billion of shareholder value.
qs.zh: 他们的干预最终创造了超过 5000 亿美元的股东价值。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: Trustworthiness is the most underrated asset in all of business.
qs.zh: 可信度是所有商业中最被低估的资产。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: If you're serious about being mission driven, you have to show me that you cannot profit except by achieving the mission.
qs.zh: 如果你真的对使命驱动很认真，你必须向我表明，除非实现使命，否则你就无法盈利。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: Only make deposits, never make withdrawals.
qs.zh: 只做存款，绝不做取款。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: The problem is if a company can be decapitated at any time, you can no longer trust it.
qs.zh: 问题在于，如果一家公司随时可能被斩首，你就再也无法信任它了。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: Corporations, organizations are the oldest form of artificial intelligence on the planet.
qs.zh: 公司、组织是地球上最古老的人工智能形式。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

qs.en: The more ants you put in the puzzle, the faster the solution. But the more humans you add, the worse, unless the humans are very carefully aligned.
qs.zh: 你在谜题中放入的蚂蚁越多，解决速度越快。但是你增加的人类越多，情况越糟，除非这些人类非常仔细地对齐。
qs.speaker: Eric Ries

tldr: 创始人如何用法律结构和使命驱动，保护公司免受短期利润的侵蚀。

title: 对话 Notion 产品负责人 Max:AI 时代的产品方法论与人的主观能动性
desc: 前 GitHub 设计主管、现 Notion 产品负责人 Max Schoening 谈 AI 如何重塑产品构建、角色边界与可塑软件。
q: 重要的是能动性，我不认为能动性在世界上分布得很均匀。

qs.en: The thing that matters is agency, and I don't think agency is very evenly distributed in the world.
qs.zh: 重要的是能动性，我不认为能动性在世界上分布得很均匀。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: Malleable software is the idea that software works closer to the interest of the people that use it than the interest of the corporation that makes it, maybe that's how I'd frame it.
qs.zh: 可塑软件的理念是，软件更贴近使用者的利益，而不是制造它的公司的利益，也许这就是我的框架。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: I think to some degree the SaaS apocalypse is greatly exaggerated.
qs.zh: 我认为在某种程度上 SaaS 末日被大大夸大了。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: I think the first 10% of every project are now free.
qs.zh: 我认为每个项目的前 10% 现在是免费的。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: One of the biggest pitfalls is if you get into the loop of, if I just add one more thing to the product, it'll be finally great.
qs.zh: 最大的陷阱之一是如果你陷入这个循环：如果我再给产品添加一样东西，它最终就会变得很棒。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: If I really look at the truly great products, they all have one tiny core that is so exceptionally good.
qs.zh: 如果我真正看看那些真正伟大的产品，它们都有一个非常小的核心，那是极其出色的。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: Taste actually means you're able to run a virtual machine in your head where given an idea, you can predict for a certain in group whether they're going to like it or not.
qs.zh: 品味实际上意味着你能够在脑海中运行一台虚拟机，给定一个想法，你可以预测某个特定群体是否会喜欢它。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: My take is that we already have universal basic income. It's called knowledge work.
qs.zh: 我的观点是我们已经有了全民基本收入，它叫作知识工作。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

qs.en: One day you wake up and you realize the world is made up by people no smarter than you.
qs.zh: 有一天你醒来，你会意识到这个世界是由并不比你聪明的人组成的。
qs.speaker: Max Schoening

tldr: 前 GitHub 设计主管、现 Notion 产品负责人 Max Schoening 谈 AI 如何重塑产品构建、角色边界与可塑软件。

title: Snap 创始人 Evan Spiegel:做硬件、搞创新、用 AI,为什么人性比技术更重要
desc: Snap CEO 谈软件不是护城河、硬件为何重要,以及如何用扁平设计团队持续创新。
q: 15 年前，我们基本上认识到软件不是护城河，这是今天每个人都在随着 AI 发现的事情。

qs.en: 15 years ago, we essentially learned that software is not a moat, which is something that everyone is discovering today with AI.
qs.zh: 15 年前，我们基本上认识到软件不是护城河，这是今天每个人都在随着 AI 发现的事情。
qs.speaker: Evan Spiegel

qs.en: So it's very easy to copy software features. It's very hard to copy or to replicate a full ecosystem or a platform.
qs.zh: 复制软件功能很容易。复制或重现完整的生态系统或平台是非常困难的。
qs.speaker: Evan Spiegel

qs.en: a lot of our designers are now shipping code, which is extraordinary.
qs.zh: 我们的许多设计师现在正在发布代码，这是非同寻常的。
qs.speaker: Evan Spiegel

qs.en: I remember I had the opportunity to meet President Clinton at one point in the early days of the company and he was like, "It's very interesting, being president is really being explainer in chief and your job is actually to just explain stuff to people and help them make sense of the world and the company and their role in it."
qs.zh: 我记得在公司早期我有机会见到克林顿总统，他说，「做总统很有趣，其实就是要做首席解释官，你的工作实际上就是向人们解释事情，帮助他们理解世界、公司以及他们在其中的角色。」
qs.speaker: Evan Spiegel

qs.en: humanity is far more important than the technological developments, largely because humanity dictates how technology is adopted.
qs.zh: 人性远比技术发展更重要，很大程度上因为人性决定了技术如何被采用。
qs.speaker: Evan Spiegel

qs.en: you have two ears and one mouth. Use them in that proportion.
qs.zh: 你有两只耳朵和一张嘴。按那个比例使用它们。
qs.speaker: Evan Spiegel

tldr: Snap CEO 谈软件不是护城河、硬件为何重要,以及如何用扁平设计团队持续创新。

title: AI 时代产品经理生存指南：一半人将被迫转行，一半人迎来复兴
desc: 前 Meta、Google 高管 Nikhyl Singhal 断言：PM 行业正在大洗牌，未来两年唯有成为拥抱 AI 的「构建者」才能生存。
q: 总的来说，这个职能已经变得极其专注于没有权力的责任。

qs.en: Generally, the function had become extremely focused on responsibility without authority.
qs.zh: 总的来说，这个职能已经变得极其专注于没有权力的责任。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: But you might see a company shed 30,000 and hire 8,000, but the 8,000 people they're going to hire are going to all be AI first.
qs.zh: 但你可能会看到一家公司裁掉 30,000 人，然后招聘 8,000 人，但他们要招聘的这 8,000 人将全部是 AI 优先的。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: I think that there will be 10 to a hundred times more changes that will be presented to products than ever before, because now the cost of testing something, the cost of changing is going to be much, much lower.
qs.zh: 我认为，与以往相比，产品将面临 10 倍到 100 倍更多的变化，因为现在测试某事的成本、变更的成本将大大降低。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: The information mover is essentially going to become a dinosaur.
qs.zh: 信息搬运工基本上将变成恐龙。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: I think that one of the most surprising shifts we're seeing is your brands don't matter as much as how modern you are in your ability to deliver product.
qs.zh: 我认为我们看到的最令人惊讶的转变之一是，你的品牌并不如你在交付产品方面的现代化程度重要。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: And the most surprising observation I made is that the ones that were the best at working in the past, the ones that mastered the old game, find it the hardest to go through this reinvention stage.
qs.zh: 我做过的最令人惊讶的观察是，那些过去最擅长工作的人，那些掌握了旧游戏规则的人，发现最难度过这个重塑阶段。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: And my dad's definition is still my favorite, which is an engineer is someone who obsoletes themselves from everything they do.
qs.zh: 他说，我爸爸的定义仍然是我最喜欢的，即工程师是一个让自己从所做的每件事中过时的人。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

qs.en: Genius is 1% inspiration, 99% perspiration.
qs.zh: 天才是 1% 的灵感，99% 的汗水。
qs.speaker: Nikhyl Singhal

tldr: 前 Meta、Google 高管 Nikhyl Singhal 断言：PM 行业正在大洗牌，未来两年唯有成为拥抱 AI 的「构建者」才能生存。

title: Keith Rabois 的用人铁律：别招熟手、别做客户访谈、公开批评
desc: 从 PayPal 黑帮到顶级 VC，Keith Rabois 讲透了如何识别顶尖人才、如何在 AI 时代重构团队。
q: 你建立的团队就是你建立的公司。

qs.en: The team you build is the company you build.
qs.zh: 你建立的团队就是你建立的公司。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: I think you have to build a company on undiscovered talent.
qs.zh: 我认为你必须建立在未被发现的才华之上。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: The single role for the CEO is offsetting that complacency.
qs.zh: CEO 的唯一角色就是抵消那种自满。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: And the morale actually does go down for the best people in the world when people are skating.
qs.zh: 当人们在滑行（摸鱼）时，世界上最好的人的士气确实会下降。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: What I've noticed in some of the best organizations is the number one consumer of tokens is the CMO
qs.zh: 我注意到在一些最好的组织里，token 的第一大消耗者是 CMO
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: he convinced me that the idea of a PM makes no sense basically in the future.
qs.zh: 他让我相信，PM 这个概念在未来基本上讲不通。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: the capabilities of foundation models or companies like Lovable and things like that are just so improving such a rapid rate that it makes no sense to have a year-long roadmap.
qs.zh: 基础模型的能力或像 Lovable 这样的公司的能力正以如此快的速度提升，以至于制定一个为期一年的路线图毫无意义。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: he personally ships as much code as he used to as an individual contributor while he's managing a team of 20 because the tools are so great and he's become a leading pioneer in the usage of AI.
qs.zh: 在管理一个 20 人团队的同时，他个人提交的代码量和他作为独立贡献者时一样多，因为工具太棒了，而且他已成为使用 AI 的领军先驱。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: 99% of the time they will tell you every reason except the real reason.
qs.zh: 99% 的时间他们会告诉你除了真实原因之外的每一个原因。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

qs.en: High performance machines don't have psychological safety.
qs.zh: 高性能机器没有心理安全感。
qs.speaker: Keith Rabois

tldr: 从 PayPal 黑帮到顶级 VC，Keith Rabois 讲透了如何识别顶尖人才、如何在 AI 时代重构团队。

title: Anthropic 增长负责人：用 Claude 自动化增长实验，把 PM 的活交给工程师
desc: 在增长快到「线性图都不酷了」的 Anthropic，增长团队用 AI 自动跑实验、让工程师当 mini-PM，还坚持把安全和品牌置于短期指标之上。
q: 你需要明白，你过去 50%、60%、70% 的运作方式，直接把它们抛在脑后吧。

qs.en: You need to understand that 50%, 60%, 70% of how you operate in the past, just throw it out the door.
qs.zh: 你需要明白，你过去 50%、60%、70% 的运作方式，直接把它们抛在脑后吧。
qs.speaker: Amol Avasare

qs.en: The product value that we will deliver in two years time is probably like 1000X, what it is today.
qs.zh: 我们两年后将交付的产品价值可能是今天的 1000 倍。
qs.speaker: Amol Avasare

qs.en: I'm averse to PRDs. I think I just hate documentation.
qs.zh: 我反感 PRD。我想我只是讨厌文档。
qs.speaker: Amol Avasare

qs.en: we had ultimately chosen not to launch it for safety reasons. I think the team didn't want to kick off effectively like an AI global arms race.
qs.zh: 我们最终选择了不推出它，出于安全原因。我认为团队不想有效地引发一场 AI 全球军备竞赛。
qs.speaker: Amol Avasare

qs.en: And I think in growth, I think it's really important that you just need to be okay leaving money on the table.
qs.zh: 我认为在增长中，我认为非常重要的是你需要愿意把钱留在桌上。
qs.speaker: Amol Avasare

tldr: 在增长快到「线性图都不酷了」的 Anthropic，增长团队用 AI 自动跑实验、让工程师当 mini-PM，还坚持把安全和品牌置于短期指标之上。

title: OpenClaw 深度玩法：三任 CPO 的九个智能体实战心得
desc: 从最早期把日历删光的怀疑者，到给九个智能体各配角色的重度玩家，Claire Vo 完整复盘 OpenClaw 的安装、避坑与日常用法。
q: 我认为人们在 OpenClaw 上跌跌撞撞的部分原因是，他们读到 OpenClaw 正在经营我的业务，他们以为可以把任何任务扔给单个智能体并获得出色的结果。

qs.en: Part of I think where people stumble with OpenClaw is they read about OpenClaw is running my business, and they think they can throw any task at a single agent and get great results.
qs.zh: 我认为人们在 OpenClaw 上跌跌撞撞的部分原因是，他们读到 OpenClaw 正在经营我的业务，他们以为可以把任何任务扔给单个智能体并获得出色的结果。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: we're going to have to rethink what is the interface of the web to be more agent friendly because I think we skip ahead a couple years and the number one user of websites are going to be people's agents.
qs.zh: 我们将不得不重新思考什么是网络的界面，以变得更对智能体友好，因为我认为我们快进几年，网站的第一大用户将会是人们的智能体。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: the highest bandwidth API for an LLM is just chatting to it.
qs.zh: LLM 的最高带宽 API 就是和它聊天。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: just bringing this manager's mindset to how you use these things, how you scope their roles, how you onboard them, how you onboard them technically, how you train them, how you give them more trust, I say bring those skills into it, again, not because we're going to personify the AI agents, but because I think that is why I have been so successful with these tools is because I have 20 years plus of management experience.
qs.zh: 只是把这种管理者的心态带入你如何使用这些东西，如何界定他们的范围，如何让他们入职，如何在技术上让他们入职，如何培训他们，如何给他们更多信任，我说把这些技能带进来，再次强调，不是因为我们拟人化 AI 智能体，而是我认为这就是我在这些工具上如此成功的原因是因为我有 20 年以上的管理经验。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: I'm having this, which I have not had since ChatGPT came out, which is this is going to change everything.
qs.zh: 我正在经历这个，自从 ChatGPT 出现以来我还没有过这种时刻，就是这将改变一切。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: most people you work with won't be at your funeral.
qs.zh: 大多数和你一起工作的人不会出现在你的葬礼上。
qs.speaker: Claire Vo

qs.en: The only people that will remember that you stayed late at work are your kids.
qs.zh: 唯一会记得你工作到很晚的人是你的孩子。
qs.speaker: Lenny

tldr: 从最早期把日历删光的怀疑者，到给九个智能体各配角色的重度玩家，Claire Vo 完整复盘 OpenClaw 的安装、避坑与日常用法。

title: 别只想推销：产品负责人如何真正影响高管决策
desc: 产品负责人掌握影响力的核心，是理解高管的处境与目标，用同理心引导他们为好想法买账。
q: 而来参加那个产品评审的产品经理，或者是试图做推介的领导者，心里想的是，“为了这次会议我已经准备了两周、三周，也许自从我们上次说话以来已经六周了，”但走进那个会议的高管从那以后就没想过你。

qs.en: And the product manager coming to that product review, or the leader who's trying to make a pitch, thinks, "I've been prepping for this meeting for two weeks, three weeks, maybe six weeks since we last spoke," but the executive coming into that session hasn't thought about you since.
qs.zh: 而来参加那个产品评审的产品经理，或者是试图做推介的领导者，心里想的是，“为了这次会议我已经准备了两周、三周，也许自从我们上次说话以来已经六周了，”但走进那个会议的高管从那以后就没想过你。
qs.speaker: Jessica Fain

qs.en: The other thing I always tell people I managed is, it's your fault if the leaders didn't buy into your idea.
qs.zh: 我总是告诉我管理的人的另一件事是，如果领导者不认同你的想法，那是你的错。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: Politics is manipulating outcomes and people for your own gain. Influence is about increasing the odds that your good ideas survive.
qs.zh: 政治是为了自己的利益操纵结果和他人。影响力是增加你的好想法存活下来的几率。
qs.speaker: Jessica Fain

qs.en: I think one of the most disastrous things you can do is going into a meeting just looking for approval for your plan.
qs.zh: 我认为你可以做的最灾难性的事情之一就是带着仅仅寻求计划批准的目的去参加会议。
qs.speaker: Jessica Fain

qs.en: what I find is that people don't take the bait. And the best people do.
qs.zh: 我发现的是人们没有上钩。最优秀的人会。
qs.speaker: Jessica Fain

qs.en: I think one of the biggest things you can do to build trust is kill things, deprioritize things.
qs.zh: 我认为建立信任你能做的最重要的事情之一就是砍掉东西，降低优先级。
qs.speaker: Jessica Fain

qs.en: The act of stakeholder management, the act of learning is the 10X skill.
qs.zh: 利益相关者管理的行為，学习的行為，是 10 倍效能的技能。
qs.speaker: Jessica Fain

tldr: 产品负责人掌握影响力的核心，是理解高管的处境与目标，用同理心引导他们为好想法买账。

title: 1500 亿美元的隐形 AI 公司创始人：恐惧源于无知，最好的工作是独自安静地完成
desc: Applied Intuition CEO Qasar Younis 谈物理 AI、对抗焦虑与务实创业。
q: 如果你在家对 AI 感到非常焦虑，你能做的最好的事情就是花时间去理解，你很快就会看到它的局限性。

qs.en: If you at home are very anxious about AI, the best thing that you can do is spend time to understand and you will quickly see the limitations.
qs.zh: 如果你在家对 AI 感到非常焦虑，你能做的最好的事情就是花时间去理解，你很快就会看到它的局限性。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: Us solving some of these impossible problems like cancer are directly going to be related to this AI boom.
qs.zh: 我们解决一些像癌症这样的不可能的问题，将直接与这次 AI 繁荣有关。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: you realize that you can see the video of nunchuck wielding humanoids, which are pre-programmed and that costs $15 million to do that video.
qs.zh: 你意识到你能看到挥舞双截棍的人形机器人的视频，它们是预先编程的，制作那个视频花费了 1500 万美元。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: just in the United States, over 30,000 people will die in the next year from these accidents.
qs.zh: 仅在美国，明年将有超过 30,000 人死于这些事故。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: The real impact of AI in the next 5 to 10 years really is going to be in farming, mining, construction.
qs.zh: AI 在未来 5 到 10 年的真正影响将真正是在农业、采矿和建筑领域。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: All of our company values can be reduced to these two words of radical pragmatism.
qs.zh: 我们所有的公司价值观都可以归结为这两个词：激进实用主义。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: Every minute you're writing something for public consumption, you're not focusing your very limited time that you have on your customers and your product.
qs.zh: 你每一分钟都在为公共消费写东西，你就没有把你非常有限的时间集中在你的客户和产品上。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: Read old books because time has filtered out a lot of the noise.
qs.zh: 读旧书，因为时间已经过滤掉了许多噪音。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

qs.en: technical mastery is mastering the complex, and I think computers do that really well, and creativity is mastering the simple.
qs.zh: 技术精通是掌握复杂，我认为计算机做得很好，而创造力是掌握简单。
qs.speaker: Qasar Younis

tldr: Applied Intuition CEO Qasar Younis 谈物理 AI、对抗焦虑与务实创业。

title: The design process is dead. Here’s what’s replacing it. | Jenny Wen (head of design at Claude)
desc: Claude设计负责人Jenny Wen分享AI时代设计流程剧变:旧流程已死,设计师从画图者转向愿景领航员与代码实现者。
q: 我认为它在 AI 时代之前就已经在消亡了,但既然现在工程师可以离开并启动他们的七个 Claude,我认为作为设计师,我们真的必须放弃那个流程。

qs.en: I think it was sort of dying before the age of AI, but given now that engineers can go off and spin off their seven Claudes, I think as designers, we really have to let go of that process.
qs.zh: 我认为它在 AI 时代之前就已经在消亡了,但既然现在工程师可以离开并启动他们的七个 Claude,我认为作为设计师,我们真的必须放弃那个流程。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

qs.en: At the end of the day, someone has to decide what is actually going to get built and what actually matters.
qs.zh: 归根结底,必须有人决定实际要构建什么以及什么真正重要。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

qs.en: Or given what the AI is presenting us, someone still needs to be accountable for the decision.
qs.zh: 或者鉴于 AI 展示给我们的东西,仍然需要有人对决定负责。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

qs.en: I think that what will probably happen here, is that a lot of those UIs will be generated more and more often by the models, as opposed to something that we're hand coding each instance.
qs.zh: 我认为这里可能会发生的是,这些 UI 中的大多数将越来越多地由模型生成,而不是我们要为每个实例手工编码。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

qs.en: if both the founder and idea is super legible, the idea is probably not that novel, and somebody's already like, they're already going to implement it or do it and you're actually not finding something new.
qs.zh: 如果创始人和想法都是超级可读的,那么这个想法可能不那么新颖,已经有人像那样要去实施它或做它了,而你实际上没有发现什么新东西。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

qs.en: And I think this person is really interesting right now because I think most companies are just hiring senior talent, folks that have done things before, are super experienced, but given how much the roles are changing and what we're expected to do is changing, I think having somebody who almost has a blank slate, and is just a really quick learner and is really eager to learn new tactics and stuff like that, and doesn't have all these baked in processes and rituals in their mind, that's super valuable.
qs.zh: 我认为这个人现在真的很有趣,因为我认为大多数公司只是招聘高级人才,那些以前做过事情的人,非常有经验的人,但考虑到角色的变化程度以及我们要做的事情的变化程度,我认为拥有一个几乎是白纸一张的人,是一个非常快速的学习者,并且非常渴望学习新战术和类似的东西,并且脑海中没有所有这些既定的流程和仪式,这是非常有价值的。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

qs.en: But when I think about leaders and managers that I respect the most, I actually think some of their best traits is that they choose low leverage tasks that they take on themselves, and that actually ends up being actually a very high leverage thing, because it's them who's doing it.
qs.zh: 但当我想到我最尊敬的领导者和经理时,我实际上认为他们最好的特质之一是他们选择自己承担的低杠杆任务,而这最终实际上是一件非常高杠杆的事情,因为是他们在做。
qs.speaker: Jenny Wen

tldr: Claude设计负责人Jenny Wen分享AI时代设计流程剧变:旧流程已死,设计师从画图者转向愿景领航员与代码实现者。

title: 对话 Cisco CPO Jeetu Patel:大公司如何不掉队 AI 时代
desc: Cisco 产品一号位亲述:大企业如何从顶层决心转型 AI、放下自我,以及平台与时机为何决定个人成败。
q: 大多数人在大公司里认为的是大公司不进行实验。事实上并非如此。大公司经常进行实验。大公司不做的是当一个实验成功时,他们不会全力以赴并加倍下注。

qs.en: Most people think in large companies is large companies don't experiment. That is in fact not true. Large companies experiment a lot. What large companies don't do is when an experiment works, they don't go all in and double down.
qs.zh: 大多数人在大公司里认为的是大公司不进行实验。事实上并非如此。大公司经常进行实验。大公司不做的是当一个实验成功时,他们不会全力以赴并加倍下注。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: But the reverse was guaranteed to be the case, that if you didn't choose AI, if you weren't going to be dexterous in whatever job function you're doing, then your job is probably not going to be that relevant over here in the long run.
qs.zh: 但反过来是必然的,如果你不选择 AI,如果你在你的任何工作职能中不灵活,那么你的工作在长远来看可能不会那么相关。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: We have to become not a holding company of 251 acquisitions and thousands of different products, we have to become a platform company.
qs.zh: 我们绝不能成为一家拥有 251 次收购和数千种不同产品的控股公司,我们必须成为一家平台公司。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: If these GPUs aren't networked together, you don't have AI, because it used to be that you could train a model on a single GPU, but then what happened was the model got too big to be put on a single GPU.
qs.zh: 如果这些 GPU 没有联网在一起,你就没有 AI,因为过去你可以在单个 GPU 上训练一个模型,但后来发生的事情是模型变得太大,无法放在单个 GPU 上。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: That requires a very sophisticated set of technologies that we build to make sure that you could have two data centers, 800 kilometers apart, but boy, they run completely in sync with each other.
qs.zh: 这需要一套非常复杂的技术,我们要构建这些技术,以确保你可以有两个相距 800 公里的数据中心,但是,它们运行起来完全同步。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: When that's not the case, we worry about AI taking our jobs, I think that survival of humanity depends on a successful AI.
qs.zh: 当情况不再如此时,我们担心 AI 夺走我们的工作,我认为人类的生存取决于成功的 AI。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: And the thing that I learned about infrastructure is, you don't always get the glory, but you always get the blame.
qs.zh: 我学到的关于基础设施的一点是,你并不总是能得到荣耀,但你总是会得到指责。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: Because if you have 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 layers between you and the person who's actually doing the job in the front line, what you don't want to do is play the telephone game and assume that people will just cascade it
qs.zh: 因为如果在你和实际在一线工作的人之间隔着 3、4、5、6、7 层,你不想做的就是玩传话游戏,并假设人们只会层层传递
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: Because when the infrastructure doesn't work, people die. Someone doesn't get dialysis, someone doesn't get a surgery done, and we need to make sure that we're working with someone with the infrastructure is working.
qs.zh: 因为当基础设施不工作时,人会死。有人没法做透析,有人没法做手术,我们需要确保我们正在与基础设施工作正常的人合作。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: If you don't care about who gets the credit, you just go a lot farther in life.
qs.zh: 如果你不在乎谁得到功劳,你在生活中会走得远得多。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: Because even my mother that knows me inside and out didn't know how much I loved her, that there's no chance that people in the business world are going to know how you feel if you're not explicit with them.
qs.zh: 因为即使是那个里里外外了解我的母亲都不知道我有多爱她,那么如果你在商业世界中不明确表达,那些人就没有机会知道你的感觉。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: I'm like, "This guy is smarter than every person on the executive team and probably just as smart as every salesperson we have, but he's making $10 a day and all of us are enjoying this amazing life, and it's because we have access to a platform and he doesn't."
qs.zh: 我说,「这家伙比高管团队的每个人都聪明,可能跟我们要有的每个销售人员一样聪明,但他一天赚 10 美元,而我们都在享受这美好的生活,这是因为我们有平台可以使用,而他没有。」
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: It's the most important. It's the thing that you control the least. And there's a lot of companies that have built amazing products, amazing services at the wrong time, in the right market and not won, right?
qs.zh: 它是最重要的。它是你控制得最少的东西。有很多公司在错误的时候建立了惊人的产品、惊人的服务,在正确的市场却没有赢,对吧?
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: If you have a great market mediocre team, the market pulls you up. If you have a shitty market and a great team, the market drags you down. The market always wins.
qs.zh: 不,如果你有一个伟大的市场和普通的团队,市场会把你拉上来。如果你有一个糟糕的市场和一个伟大的团队,市场会把你拖下去。市场总是赢家。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

qs.en: When you feel like you need a PhD to understand what someone's saying, chances are it ain't going to be a megatrend, because by definition, a megatrend is it's going to impact a large population of the world.
qs.zh: 当你觉得你需要有个博士学位才能理解某人在说什么时,它大概率不会是一个超级趋势,因为根据定义,超级趋势是它将影响世界上很大一部分人口。
qs.speaker: Jeetu Patel

tldr: Cisco 产品一号位亲述:大企业如何从顶层决心转型 AI、放下自我,以及平台与时机为何决定个人成败。

title: 育儿专家 Dr. Becky 谈职场领导力：怎么管“大号婴儿”
desc: 临床心理学家 Dr. Becky 将育儿原则迁移到职场，教你如何修复关系、设定界限并建立长期韧性。
q: 我认为修复是我们拥有的头号关系策略。

qs.en: I think repair is kind of the number one relationship strategy we have.
qs.zh: 我认为修复是我们拥有的头号关系策略。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: Secure attachment is just defined by, we're all going to mess up, but secure attachment has an adult who's willing to repair?
qs.zh: 安全依恋仅仅是由，我们都会搞砸，但安全依恋中有一个成年人愿意修复？
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: We feel people's intention, not just their intervention.
qs.zh: 我们感觉到的是人们的意图，而不仅仅是他们的干预。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: The idea of being good inside inherently requires us to separate behavior and identity.
qs.zh: “内心是好的”这一理念本质上要求我们将行为和身份区分开来。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: The quickest way to have an unproductive conversation is to lose sight of the fact that someone's good inside.
qs.zh: 进行一次无成效对话的最快方式，就是忽略某人内心是善良的这一事实。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: You inherently cannot be judgmental when you're curious. And when you're judgmental about something, you're inherently not curious about it.
qs.zh: 当你感到好奇时，你天生就无法做出评判。当你对某事做出评判时，你天生就对它没有好奇心。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: Bad behavior at any age can basically be reduced to feelings that overpower skills.
qs.zh: 任何年龄的不良行为基本上都可以归结为感觉压倒了技能。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: Boundaries are what you tell someone else you will do, and it requires the other person to do nothing.
qs.zh: 界限是你告诉别人你会做什么，它要求对方什么都不做。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

qs.en: This feels hard because it is hard, not because I'm doing something wrong.
qs.zh: 这感觉很难，是因为它本来就难，而不是因为我做错了什么。
qs.speaker: Dr. Becky Kennedy

tldr: 临床心理学家 Dr. Becky 将育儿原则迁移到职场，教你如何修复关系、设定界限并建立长期韧性。

title: 增长停滞怎么办？Jason Cohen 的四步诊断法
desc: 从流失率、定价、净收入留存到渠道饱和度，按序排查增长瓶颈。
q: 你的价格太低了，因为你只是猜的，而且你从未改变过它们。

qs.en: Your prices are way too low because you just guessed and you haven't changed them.
qs.zh: 你的价格太低了，因为你只是猜的，而且你从未改变过它们。
qs.speaker: Jason Cohen

qs.en: Your prices are way too low because you just guessed and you haven't changed them.
qs.zh: 你的价格太低了，因为你只是瞎猜的，而且你没有改变过它们。
qs.speaker: Jason Cohen

qs.en: quality is actually the only thing that matters and the consistency doesn't matter.
qs.zh: 质量实际上是唯一重要的事情，而一致性并不重要。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: So a company like that will never have more than 2,000 customers.
qs.zh: 所以像这样的公司永远不会有超过 2,000 个客户。
qs.speaker: Jason Cohen

qs.en: how this company was able to charge eight times as much for the same product just by talking about it differently.
qs.zh: 这家公司如何能够通过用不同的方式谈论同一个产品而收取八倍的价格。
qs.speaker: Jason Cohen

tldr: 从流失率、定价、净收入留存到渠道饱和度，按序排查增长瓶颈。

title: 非技术 PM 的 AI 独立开发术：从 Cursor 到「智能体同行评审」
desc: 完全不懂代码的 PM 分享如何用 AI 搭建赚钱产品并保持代码质量。
q: 如果人们离开时觉得你多么了不起，你就失败了。如果人们离开后打开他们的电脑并开始构建，你就成功了。

qs.en: If people walk away thinking how amazing you are, you failed. And if people walk away and open their computer and start building, you've succeeded.
qs.zh: 如果人们离开时觉得你多么了不起，你就失败了。如果人们离开后打开他们的电脑并开始构建，你就成功了。
qs.speaker: Zevi Arnovitz

qs.en: Yeah, and I think this is the big difference between just vibe coding and going along with the vibes and really building serious apps.
qs.zh: 是的，我认为这就是单纯的 vibe coding 和顺其自然与真正构建严肃应用之间的巨大区别。
qs.speaker: Zevi Arnovitz

qs.en: I was building, I was fully localizing StudyMate from Hebrew to English, which I did in two days, which would probably take a dev team weeks.
qs.zh: 我正在构建，我正在把 StudyMate 从希伯来语完全本地化到英语，我在两天内完成了，这可能需要一个开发团队几周的时间。
qs.speaker: Zevi Arnovitz

qs.en: Going back to your prompts, understanding what was not good enough, iterating on them and then seeing how AI's responses get better, I think that's probably one of the most important things and one of the things that divides between people who are okay with using AI and the people who actually know how to use it.
qs.zh: 回到你的提示词，去理解哪些不够好，对其进行迭代，然后看看 AI 的响应如何变好，我认为这可能是最重要的事情之一，也是区分那些还可以使用 AI 的人和真正知道如何使用 AI 的人的因素之一。
qs.speaker: Zevi Arnovitz

qs.en: It's you'll be replaced by someone who's better at using AI than you.
qs.zh: 取代你的是那些比你更擅长使用 AI 的人。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: Yeah, I think titles are going to collapse and responsibilities are going to collapse and everyone's just going to be building.
qs.zh: 是的，我认为头衔将会崩塌，责任将会崩塌，每个人都将只是在构建。
qs.speaker: Zevi Arnovitz

qs.en: I think that there's a misconception with a lot of PMs that the job is always having the right answers and being the smartest person in the room.
qs.zh: 我认为许多 PM 有一个误解，认为工作总是拥有正确的答案并成为房间里最聪明的人。
qs.speaker: Zevi Arnovitz

tldr: 完全不懂代码的 PM 分享如何用 AI 搭建赚钱产品并保持代码质量。

title: 1.2 个人 + 20 个 AI 智能体：SaaStr 的极简销售实验
desc: SaaStr 创始人用 20 个智能体替代约 10 人销售团队，详解 AI 落地 GTM 的实战经验。
q: 我真的无法每年付给一个初级 SDR 15 万美元结果他们却辞职。

qs.en: I just can't pay a junior SDR $150,000 a year to quit.
qs.zh: 我真的无法每年付给一个初级 SDR 15 万美元结果他们却辞职。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: The email-based cadence SDR will be 90% displaced by AI next year.
qs.zh: 基于邮件节奏的 SDR 明年将被 AI 取代 90%。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: AI is replacing the jobs people don't want to do today, and it is displacing the mid-pack and the mediocre.
qs.zh: AI 正在取代人们今天不想做的工作，并且它正在挤出中游和平庸的人。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: if Lenny rocks and the other vendor is better and won't help you, don't do it.
qs.zh: 如果 Lenny 很棒，而另一个供应商更好但不会帮你，那就别做。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: Being the orchestrator or the chief AI person is not a good job for lazy people because the agents never sleep.
qs.zh: 做编排者或首席 AI 人员对于懒人来说不是一份好工作，因为智能体从不睡觉。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: Business process change at the end of the day, and so many founders get this wrong, and 99% of sales folks, they don't care about business process change.
qs.zh: 业务流程变更归根结底，这么多创始人搞错了这一点，99% 的销售人员，他们不在乎业务流程变更。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: Take your best person on your sales team, your best marketer you have, take their email copy and use that as the template for your AI.
qs.zh: 拿你销售团队里最好的人，你拥有的最好的营销人员，拿他们的邮件文案并把它用作你的 AI 的模板。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: the bar for good enough for AI GTM, it's not as high as we think.
qs.zh: 对于 AI GTM 来说「足够好」的门槛，并没有我们想象的那么高。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: I think today, 95% of 100, you've got to promote someone internally.
qs.zh: 我认为今天，在 100 分里，你有 95 分必须从内部提拔某人。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

qs.en: Net net, we're going to need more sales and go-to-market professionals than ever because the winners are growing so quickly that even if they're more efficient, they will need more human beings than ever.
qs.zh: 总的来说，我们将需要比以往更多的销售和 go-to-market 专业人士，因为赢家增长得太快了，即使他们效率更高，他们也比以往更需要人类。
qs.speaker: Jason Lemkin

tldr: SaaStr 创始人用 20 个智能体替代约 10 人销售团队，详解 AI 落地 GTM 的实战经验。

title: Rippling高管Matt MacInnis:成就伟业,你必须时刻保持极度紧绷
desc: Rippling CPO 谈如何用极度紧绷的状态对抗组织熵增,以及何时该放弃并退出创业。
q: 对我来说,我们要感觉公司里的每一个项目都是故意人手不足的,这一点真的很重要。

qs.en: It is really important to me that we feel that we've deliberately understaffed every project at the company.
qs.zh: 对我来说,我们要感觉公司里的每一个项目都是故意人手不足的,这一点真的很重要。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: Teams will always optimize for local comfort over company outcomes.
qs.zh: 团队总是会为了局部的舒适度而优化,而不是为了公司的结果。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: Every next concentric circle of management beyond the founder CEO has the potential to be an order of magnitude drop off in intensity.
qs.zh: 创始人 CEO 之外的每一圈管理层,其强度都有可能出现一个数量级的下降。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: If they ever find themselves in the comfort zone at work, they are definitely making a mistake.
qs.zh: 如果他们在工作中发现自己处于舒适区,那他们肯定是在犯错误。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: If you leave anything on the field, if you sort of leave a crack for your competitor, 100% chance they're going to go fill that crack.
qs.zh: 如果你在场上留下了任何东西,如果你某种程度上为你的竞争对手留了一条裂缝,他们有 100% 的几率会去填满那条裂缝。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: And so it's very clear that under-staffing is less evil than over-staffing.
qs.zh: 所以很清楚,人员不足比人员过剩要小恶得多。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: You don't really learn from your mistakes, you learn from your successes.
qs.zh: 你并没有真正从你的错误中学习,你从你的成功中学习。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: Processes in a business exist for the sole purpose of lowering beta.
qs.zh: 商业中的流程存在的唯一目的就是降低 beta。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: The downside of a process is that it suppresses alpha.
qs.zh: 流程的缺点是它会抑制 alpha。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: If you hate product managers, you just haven't worked with a great product manager.
qs.zh: 如果你讨厌产品经理,你只是还没与一位优秀的产品经理合作过。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: We talk in Silicon Valley about never quit, but that is complete absolute venture capital bullshit.
qs.zh: 我们在硅谷谈论永不放弃,但这完全是绝对的风险投资狗屁废话。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: You should fucking quit. You should reset the clock, you should reset the cap table because trust me, product market fit when it arrives is insane and it's exciting and you should pursue it.
qs.zh: 你应该他妈的放弃。你应该重置时钟,你应该重置股权结构表,因为相信我,当产品市场契合度到来时,它是疯狂的且令人兴奋的,你应该去追求它。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: Don't ask people for advice, ask people for relevant experience.
qs.zh: 不要向别人征求建议,要向别人征求相关经验。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: Do not ship the product, find a lack of success, and then try to market your way through that, because the binding receptors likely don't exist
qs.zh: 不要发布产品后发现缺乏成功,然后试图通过营销来度过难关,因为受体结合很可能不存在。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

qs.en: The only antidote to entropy, the only antidote to decay in a system is energy.
qs.zh: 对抗熵的唯一解药,对抗系统中衰变的唯一解药就是能量。
qs.speaker: Matt MacInnis

tldr: Rippling CPO 谈如何用极度紧绷的状态对抗组织熵增,以及何时该放弃并退出创业。

title: Surge AI 创始人 Edwin Chen:我们教模型追逐多巴胺,而非真理
desc: 自力更生年入十亿的数据公司创始人,谈高质量数据与 AI 走偏的方向。
q: 他们认为你可以只是把人力扔向问题并获得好的数据,但这完全是错的。

qs.en: They think you could just throw bodies at a problem and get good data and that's completely wrong.
qs.zh: 他们认为你可以只是把人力扔向问题并获得好的数据,但这完全是错的。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: Yeah, so I don't trust the benchmarks at all.
qs.zh: 是的,所以我根本不信任这些基准测试。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: It's kind of crazy that these models can win IMO gold medals, but they still have trouble parsing PDFs.
qs.zh: 这些模型能获得国际数学奥林匹克竞赛金牌,但它们在解析 PDF 时仍然有困难,这有点疯狂。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: We're basically teaching our models to chase dopamine instead of truth.
qs.zh: 我们基本上是在教导我们的模型去追逐多巴胺而不是真理。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: The only way I'm going to get promoted at the end of the year is if I climb this leaderboard, even though I know that climbing it is probably going to make my model worse and accuracy
qs.zh: 我在年底获得晋升的唯一途径就是攀登这个排行榜,尽管我知道攀登它可能会让我的模型变差,而且准确性
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: If you're constantly pivoting, you're not taking any risks.
qs.zh: 如果你一直在转型,你就没有承担任何风险。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: The only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
qs.zh: 构建某种重要的、将改变世界的东西的唯一途径是,如果你找到一个你相信的大主意,并对其他所有事情说不。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: I definitely think that vibe coding is over-hyped.
qs.zh: 我绝对认为 vibe coding 被过度炒作。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

qs.en: I think one of the things that's going to happen in the next few years is that the models are actually going to become increasingly differentiated because of the personalities and behaviors that the different labs have and the kind of objective functions that they are optimizing their models for.
qs.zh: 我认为未来几年会发生的事情之一是,模型实际上将变得越来越差异化,因为不同实验室拥有的个性和行为,以及他们优化模型的目标函数类型。
qs.speaker: Edwin Chen

tldr: 自力更生年入十亿的数据公司创始人,谈高质量数据与 AI 走偏的方向。

title: 把 Go-to-Market 当产品做：Vercel COO 谈用 AI 重构销售组织
desc: 前 Stripe、现 Vercel 的 COO 分享如何用 AI 智能体重构销售流程，并将 GTM 视为产品来打造卓越体验。
q: 80% 的客户购买是为了避免痛苦或降低风险，而不是增加上行空间，

qs.en: 80% of customers buy to avoid pain or reduce risk as opposed to increase upside,
qs.zh: 80% 的客户购买是为了避免痛苦或降低风险，而不是增加上行空间，
qs.speaker: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser

qs.en: if you are an account executive in my org and I put you in front of 10 engineers at our company, it should take them 10 minutes to figure out you aren't a product manager.
qs.zh: 如果你是我组织里的客户主管，我把你放在我们公司的 10 名工程师面前，他们应该花 10 分钟才能弄清楚你不是产品经理。
qs.speaker: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser

qs.en: I think on prospecting, it can replace a fair amount because the average SDR wasn't doing overly sophisticated research in the first place.
qs.zh: 我认为在拓客方面，AI 可以取代相当大一部分，因为普通的 SDR 一开始也没有做特别复杂的研究。
qs.speaker: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser

qs.en: actually, you lost because you never really got in touch with the economic buyer.
qs.zh: 实际上，你输的原因是你从未真正联系到经济决策人。
qs.speaker: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser

qs.en: we may ultimately end up on, you know, better integrated agent platforms in the fullness of time. Or we may find that the CIO increasingly goes from a procurer of software to a builder of software
qs.zh: 我们最终可能会在时机成熟时使用更好的集成智能体平台。或者我们可能会发现 CIO 越来越从软件的采购者变成软件的构建者
qs.speaker: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser

qs.en: yeses are great, noes are great, maybes will kill you.
qs.zh: “是”很棒，“不”很棒，“也许”会毁了你。
qs.speaker: Jeanne DeWitt Grosser

tldr: 前 Stripe、现 Vercel 的 COO 分享如何用 AI 智能体重构销售流程，并将 GTM 视为产品来打造卓越体验。

title: 别再充当团队的“答案机”：高管教练 Rachel Lockett 的领导力实战课
desc: 高管教练拆解从“大包大揽”到“赋能团队”的领导力转变：辅导、优势设计与沟通框架。
q: 但伟大的领导者知道，当你试图一直提供建议并给出答案时，你实际上并没有装备你的团队去解决难题。

qs.en: But great leaders know that when you try to advise and have the answer all the time, you're not actually equipping your team to go solve the hard problems.
qs.zh: 但伟大的领导者知道，当你试图一直提供建议并给出答案时，你实际上并没有装备你的团队去解决难题。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: But when you're leading a quickly-scaling company, you quickly have less context than the people you're around.
qs.zh: 但是，当你领导一家快速扩张的公司时，你很快就会比你周围的人拥有更少的背景信息。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: There's a quote, "Most people aren't listening. They're just waiting for their turn to talk."
qs.zh: 有一句台词，“大多数人并不是在倾听。他们只是在等待轮到自己说话。”
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: I think typically a difficult conversation arises because some feelings are coming up for you, and you have a need that's not being met.
qs.zh: 我认为通常困难对话的出现是因为你产生了某种情绪，而你的某种需求没有得到满足。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: No, your manager's job is to help you perform in the job you were hired to do. It's your job to navigate your career.
qs.zh: 不，你经理的工作是帮助你在你受聘从事的工作中表现出色。你的工作则是规划你的职业生涯。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: In fact, I know you probably know this stat, 65% of startups fail because of co-founder conflict, and co-founders are in a moment where they're trying to build the future for their business, but also trying to build their own livelihood.
qs.zh: 事实上，我知道你可能知道这个统计数据，65% 的创业公司因为联合创始人冲突而失败，联合创始人在试图为他们业务建立未来的时刻，但也试图建立他们自己的生计。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: It's almost like in a marriage you go see a couples' therapist, but you don't tell all your friends that you can't stand your partner, but it keeps you up at night.
qs.zh: 这几乎就像在婚姻中你去见夫妻治疗师，但你不会告诉你所有的朋友你无法忍受你的伴侣，但这让你彻夜难眠。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: So no model, NVC or otherwise, can fix a person who's coming in rigid and full of blame.
qs.zh: 所以没有模型，无论是 NVC 还是其他，可以修复一个带着僵化和充满责备而来的人。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

qs.en: But I want to encourage listeners to think of themselves as leaders who bring humans together to self-actualize, and that they have to actively overcome the default state, which is blind, grind, and loneliness.
qs.zh: 但我想鼓励听众将自己视为了领导者，把人们聚集在一起实现自我实现，并且他们必须主动克服默认状态，那就是盲目、苦干和孤独。
qs.speaker: Rachel Lockett

tldr: 高管教练拆解从“大包大揽”到“赋能团队”的领导力转变：辅导、优势设计与沟通框架。

title: 把自家产品骂成「一坨狗屎」：Stewart Butterfield 的产品哲学
desc: Slack 创始人谈效用曲线、匠心、别让用户思考、伪工作与创造市场的哲学。
q: 我觉得我们现在拥有的东西就是一大坨狗屎。

qs.en: I feel like what we have right now is just a giant piece of shit.
qs.zh: 我觉得我们现在拥有的东西就是一大坨狗屎。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

qs.en: And then there's some magic threshold where it produces an enormous amount of value and then continued investment doesn't really pay off.
qs.zh: 然后有一个神奇的阈值，它产生巨大的价值，但继续投资并没有真正的回报。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

qs.en: If your software stops me and asks me to make a decision and I don't really understand it, you make me feel stupid.
qs.zh: 如果你的软件阻止我并要求我做出决定，而我真的不理解它，你会让我觉得自己很蠢。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

qs.en: If you can't see almost limitless opportunities to improve, then you shouldn't be designing the product, or you shouldn't be in charge of the company, or you shouldn't almost nothing.
qs.zh: 如果你看不到几乎无限的改进机会，那么你不应该设计该产品，或者你不应该负责公司，或者你几乎不应该做任何事。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

qs.en: Everything is simple if you have no idea what you're talking about.
qs.zh: 如果你对正在谈论的事情一无所知，那么一切都是简单的。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

qs.en: And the reason I say you have to be coldly rational about it is because it's fucking humiliating.
qs.zh: 我说你必须对此保持冷酷理性的原因是因为这真他妈令人感到羞辱。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

qs.en: But by the time we got that scale, 100 times the money back for the third of a day that we were down was $8 million or something like that.
qs.zh: 但是当我们达到那个规模时，对于停机的三分之一天，100 倍的退款是 800 万美元或类似的东西。
qs.speaker: Stewart Butterfield

tldr: Slack 创始人谈效用曲线、匠心、别让用户思考、伪工作与创造市场的哲学。

title: AI 教母李飞飞:从 ImageNet 到空间智能,与首个 3D 世界模型 Marble
desc: 从 ImageNet 催生深度学习,到 World Labs 用空间智能解锁 3D 世界模型。
q: 我觉得 AGI 更多是一个营销术语,而不是科学术语,作为科学家而非技术专家来说。

qs.en: I feel AGI is more a marketing term than a scientific term as a scientist than technologist.
qs.zh: 我觉得 AGI 更多是一个营销术语,而不是科学术语,作为科学家而非技术专家来说。
qs.speaker: Dr. Fei-Fei Li

qs.en: There's nothing artificial about AI. It's inspired by people. It's created by people, and most importantly, it impacts people.
qs.zh: AI 没有任何人工的成分。它的灵感来自人。它是由人创造的,最重要的是,它影响人。
qs.speaker: Lenny

qs.en: I'm an intellectually very fearless person, and I have to say when I hire young people, I look for that because I think that's a very important quality if one wants to make a difference, is that when you want to make a difference, you have to accept that you're creating something new or you're diving into something new.
qs.zh: 我是一个在智力上非常无畏的人,我必须说当我雇佣年轻人时,我会寻找这一点,因为我认为如果一个人想要做出改变,这是一个非常重要的品质,那就是当你想要做出改变时,你必须接受你正在创造新事物或正在潜入新事物。
qs.speaker: Dr. Fei-Fei Li

qs.en: It was produced by a virtual production company. We collaborated with Sony and they use Marble scenes to shoot those videos. So we were collaborating with those technical artists and directors, and they were saying, this has cut our production time by 40X.
qs.zh: 它是由一家虚拟制作公司制作的。我们与索尼合作,他们使用 Marble 场景来拍摄那些视频。所以我们与那些技术艺术家和导演合作,他们当时说,这将我们的制作时间缩短了 40 倍。
qs.speaker: Dr. Fei-Fei Li

qs.en: I think actually the more I work in AI, the more I respect humans.
qs.zh: 我认为实际上我在 AI 领域工作得越多,我就越尊重人类。
qs.speaker: Dr. Fei-Fei Li

tldr: 从 ImageNet 催生深度学习,到 World Labs 用空间智能解锁 3D 世界模型。
